notifications.health_evidence_note: Accepted means the provider accepted the request, not that the recipient received it. Only Discord synthetic readback can be verified. Telegram and WhatsApp acceptance is not delivery proof. Send test results are separate from this history.

notify.discord_step_1: Open your Discord server, then go to Server Settings → Integrations → Webhooks.
notify.discord_step_2: Click New Webhook (or select an existing one), pick the channel it should post to.
notify.discord_step_4: Paste it into the Webhook URL field below, then Send test.
notify.telegram_step_1: In Telegram, message @BotFather and send /newbot, then follow its prompts.
notify.telegram_step_2: @BotFather replies with your bot token — copy it into the Bot token field below.
notify.telegram_step_3: Add the bot to the chat/group/channel you want alerts posted to.
notify.telegram_step_4: Send any message in that chat, then open https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/getUpdates in a browser (with your token substituted) to find "chat":{"id": …} — copy that number into Chat ID.
notify.telegram_step_5: Send test, then check the target chat or topic for the sample message. An accepted request does not confirm receipt or reading.
notify.whatsapp_step_1: Go to Meta for Developers → My Apps → create (or open) an app, then add the WhatsApp product.
notify.whatsapp_step_2: Under WhatsApp → API Setup, copy a temporary (or generate a permanent) access token into Access token below.
notify.whatsapp_step_3: On the same page, copy the Phone number ID into the field below.
notify.whatsapp_step_4: Add your own number as a recipient (API Setup → "To") and enter it, digits only with country code, in Recipient below.
notify.whatsapp_step_5: Create and get approval for a message template with an image header (recommended) — enter its name in Template name. Without a template, alerts only deliver inside the 24-hour customer-service window after the recipient last messaged your business number.
notify.whatsapp_step_6: Send test, then check the recipient’s conversation for the sample message. An accepted request is not delivery confirmation.
notify.webhook_step_1: Any endpoint that accepts a Slack- or Discord-compatible JSON POST body works here (custom scripts, Zapier, n8n, ...).
notify.webhook_step_2: Paste its URL into Webhook URL below.
notify.webhook_step_3: Enable "Include chart image" if your endpoint can handle a base64-encoded PNG field (image_png_base64); leave it off for plain-text-only receivers.
notify.webhook_step_4: Send test to check whether the endpoint accepts the request. Check any downstream delivery separately.
notify.error_discord_webhook_url: Must be a discord.com or discordapp.com webhook URL.
notify.error_whatsapp_recipient: Must be digits only (E.164 without the leading +), e.g. 15551234567.
notify.checklist_discord_webhook_permission: Confirm you have the Manage Webhooks permission on the channel the webhook was created in.
notify.checklist_discord_send_test_image: Send test and confirm the image embed actually appears in the Discord channel.
notify.checklist_discord_regen_invalidates: Remember: deleting or regenerating the webhook invalidates this URL immediately.
notify.checklist_telegram_bot_added: Invite the bot to the group (or add it as an admin for a channel).
notify.checklist_telegram_chat_id_confirmed: Message the bot first, then confirm chat_id via getUpdates (negative for groups/channels).
notify.checklist_telegram_thread_id_confirmed: For a topic-enabled group, confirm the message thread id.

billing.aws_agent_title: AWS: collect from an agent on an EC2 instance
billing.aws_agent_intro: An agent on an EC2 instance can read its own AWS account's cost from Cost Explorer with the instance's IAM role — no access key is stored anywhere. Repeat on one instance per AWS account. Cost Explorer bills $0.01 per request: the agent queries every 12 hours (about $1.20 a month).
billing.aws_agent_inactive: No agent is reporting AWS costs yet.
billing.aws_agent_step_role_title: Give the instance's IAM role read access to Cost Explorer
billing.aws_agent_step_role_body: IAM → Roles → the instance's role (or Create role → AWS service → EC2) → Add permissions → Create inline policy → JSON, with this policy. Attach the role in EC2 → Instances → Actions → Security → Modify IAM role. If Cost Explorer was never opened, enable it once in Billing → Cost Explorer.
billing.aws_agent_step_cli_title: Install the AWS CLI v2 system-wide on the instance
billing.aws_agent_step_cli_body: The agent runs as the cloud-pulse system user, so the CLI must be in /usr/local/bin (the installer's default):
billing.aws_agent_step_test_body: The first command shows the account the role belongs to; the second must print a cost. AccessDenied means the policy isn't attached to the role yet.
billing.aws_agent_step_env_title: Turn it on in the agent and restart
billing.aws_agent_step_env_body: The agent queries at startup, then every 12 hours (CP_AWS_BILLING_INTERVAL, minimum 6h). An agent reports one account: don't combine this with CP_OCI_BILLING.
billing.aws_agent_step_hub_body: The account appears under Billing accounts and on the Costs page within a minute of the restart. Refresh now asks the agent again at most every 10 minutes, since each query is billed.
billing.oci_agent_title: OCI: collect from an agent on an OCI instance
billing.oci_agent_intro: If the hub can't run the OCI CLI, an agent on any OCI instance in the tenancy can query the Usage API itself with the instance principal. No API key file is kept on the server, and the Usage API is free to call.
billing.oci_agent_inactive: No agent is reporting OCI costs yet.
billing.oci_agent_tenancy_hint: Console → profile menu → Tenancy → OCID. Fills in the commands below only; nothing is saved.
billing.oci_agent_instance_hint: Compute → Instances → your instance → OCID. On the instance: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer Oracle" http://169.254.169.254/opc/v2/instance/id
billing.oci_agent_group_hint: Any name; it only has to match between the dynamic group and the policy.
billing.oci_agent_step_group_title: Create a dynamic group for the instance
billing.oci_agent_step_group_body: Identity & Security → Domains → Default → Dynamic groups → Create dynamic group, with this matching rule:
billing.oci_agent_step_policy_title: Let the group read usage reports
billing.oci_agent_step_policy_body: Identity & Security → Policies → Create policy in the root compartment, with these statements (the first reads costs, the second the instance's monthly VNIC traffic). If the group is in a non-Default identity domain, write it as '<domain>'/'<group>'.
billing.oci_agent_step_cli_title: Install the OCI CLI system-wide on the instance
billing.oci_agent_step_cli_body: The agent runs as the cloud-pulse system user and can't use a CLI installed under a personal home directory. Install it under /opt and link it into /usr/local/bin:
billing.oci_agent_step_test_title: Test the query as the agent's user
billing.oci_agent_step_test_body: JSON output means it works. NotAuthorizedOrNotFound means the dynamic group or policy is wrong or hasn't propagated yet; wait a few minutes and retry.
billing.oci_agent_step_env_title: Turn it on in the agent and restart
billing.oci_agent_step_env_body: The agent queries once at startup, then every hour (CP_OCI_BILLING_INTERVAL, minimum 15m). If oci isn't in /usr/local/bin, /usr/bin or /bin, also set CP_OCI_CLI to its absolute path.
billing.oci_agent_step_hub_body: Keep CP_BILLING on and leave CP_OCI_TENANCY_ID unset on the hub. The OCI card on the Costs page then shows this agent's figures within a minute of the restart. Enable this on one agent per tenancy.
